narrative.intro: AMI Metals has $1.5B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date, from 9 awards with an average award size of $164M. AMI Metals obligations are up 3016758.9% year over year. The Department of Homeland Security accounts for the vast majority of FY2026 obligations at $1.5B, while the Department of Defense accounts for $13.5K. Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services is the largest NAICS market for AMI Metals at $1.5B, with Other Support Activities for Air Transportation at $13.5K. Historical obligations show small activity before FY2026: FY21 $9.8K, FY22 $165K, FY23 $109K, FY24 $346K, and FY25 $48.9K. The current-year totals are partial and reflect fiscal year to date activity. Contractors and partners evaluating AMI Metals should note the concentration of obligations in one agency and one market for the current fiscal year, and the sharp year-over-year increase in obligations.

sections.heading: Who are AMI Metals' top federal buyers?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security is AMI Metals' top buyer with $1.5B in obligations for FY2026 to date. The Department of Defense is a secondary buyer with $13.5K in FY2026 obligations. The FY2026 buying pattern shows a heavy concentration in one agency rather than a broad agency spread.

sections.heading: How concentrated are AMI Metals' obligations by market?
sections.body: Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services is AMI Metals' largest market at $1.5B for FY2026 to date. Other Support Activities for Air Transportation is a much smaller market at $13.5K. The FY2026 obligations show strong concentration in a single NAICS market.

faq.q: How much does AMI Metals make from federal contracts?
faq.a: AMI Metals has $1.5B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. AMI Metals received those obligations across 9 awards, with an average award size of $164M. Historical obligations were much smaller in prior fiscal years: FY21 $9.8K, FY22 $165K, FY23 $109K, FY24 $346K, and FY25 $48.9K.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from AMI Metals?
faq.a: The Department of Homeland Security buys most from AMI Metals, with $1.5B in FY2026 obligations. The Department of Defense is also a buyer, with $13.5K in FY2026 obligations.

faq.q: What does AMI Metals sell to the government?
faq.a: AMI Metals sells primarily into Process, Physical Distribution, and Logistics Consulting Services, with $1.5B in FY2026 obligations in that NAICS market. AMI Metals also has obligations in Other Support Activities for Air Transportation at $13.5K for FY2026.

faq.q: Which AMI Metals contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: AMI Metals has expiring-contract visibility limited in these figures, but current FY2026 obligations are concentrated in $1.5B of work for the Department of Homeland Security. The dataset does not list specific expiring contract award values beyond the FY2026 obligations shown.
